newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilectra says revs hurt by new prices.
newsitem.headline: Chilectra says revs hurt by new prices.

text.p: Chilean power distribution company Chilectra said that its operating revenues will fall by 10.8 billion pesos a year, around $26 million, as a result of new lower electricity prices.
The fall is a equivalent to a drop of 5.6 percent in the Chilectra's sales revenues.
The calculation was made by applying the new tariff formula to the company's sales in 1995, said Chilectra in a statement filed at the Stocks and Values Superintendency.
The new prices, announced by the government Wednesday, will apply from Saturday but will be backdated to November when they were originally due to come into force.
The rates were delayed by a court battle between the government and four companies, including Chilectra, over the method for setting the new prices.
Chilectra, Chile's largest power distributor, is 75 percent owned by power investment company Enersis.
